answer: In a voyage-planning agent market, every seller, whether named nebula or sparrow, must lock a $100 bond before bidding on jobs. Payment waits until submitted routes pass deterministic checks against the buyer’s stated constraints; a provably invalid route forfeits the bond. Creating names is free, but operating 1,000 fake sellers ties up $100,000, and using them to submit invalid work burns real capital rather than disposable reputations.
